proofs.full_local_argument:
Local repair, not source transcription. Imported facts are Lemma 11's limiting smallest-eigenvalue law and Lemma 13's conditional residual law, with the source Proof map above. No unrestricted version of printed Lemma 14 is used.

Finite-dimensional probabilities. For U_n~Wishart(n), write Z_n=n^2 lambda_min(U_n). Lemma 11 gives convergence in distribution to Z with density f(x)=(1+x^(-1/2)) exp(-x/2-sqrt(x))/2 for x>0. Integration yields P(Z>=x)=exp(-x/2-sqrt(x)), hence P(Z>=1)=exp(-3/2). For 0<a<1 and 0<x<a^2, f(x)>=exp(-3/2)/(2 sqrt(x)); integrating gives P(Z<=a^2)>=exp(-3/2)a. Set p0=exp(-3/2)/2. Continuity at 1 and a^2 and convergence in distribution imply that for every fixed a in (0,1) there is an integer N(a)>=1 such that for all n>=N(a), P(Z_n>=1)>=p0 and P(Z_n<=a^2)>=p0 a. Thus the two needed finite-dimensional bounds follow directly from Lemma 11, without Appendix C.1's index/event expressions. N(a) is an existence threshold, not an explicit numerical convergence bound.

Quantifiers. Fix beta in (0,1), let a=sqrt(beta)/2 and d_star(beta)=ceil(N(a)/beta). For any integer d>=d_star(beta) and integer 0<=T<=floor((1-beta)d), put m=d-T. Then m>=beta d>=N(a), m>=1 and d>=N(a). Constants p0 and c=p0^2/4 are universal, independent of beta,d,T and the algorithm.

Algorithm reduction. Condition on the independent random seed R, including output randomization. Decompose each proposed query into its projection on previous orthonormal queries and a perpendicular component. Linearity supplies the projected response from known responses. A nonzero perpendicular component requires one normalized new query; a zero component requires none. This simulates the original algorithm using at most T orthonormal queries with exactly the same output. After simulation, pad to exactly T orthonormal queries by measurable choices of unused directions and ignore these extra responses. Padding is possible since T<d. For T=0 use the empty transcript. Lemma 13 applies for each fixed R. Let H include R and the padded transcript; output L is H-measurable.

Conditional residual. Lemma 13 and Appendix C.2 rotate W into M=[[AA^T,AB^T],[BA^T,BB^T+S]], with A of size T by T, B of size m by T and PSD residual S. Conditional on H, U=(d/m)S has Wishart(m) law. This law is constant in H, including the fixed seed; therefore lambda_min(S) is independent of H. Conditioning on R preserves the input Wishart law. For T=0 take S=W.

PSD comparison with singular cases. If T=0, equality holds. If T>0 and A is singular, choose nonzero u in ker(A^T); then M[u;0]=0. Since M=[A;B][A;B]^T+diag(0,S) is PSD, lambda_min(M)=0<=lambda_min(S). If A is invertible, choose a unit eigenvector v of S for s=lambda_min(S)>=0 and set z=[-A^(-T)B^T v;v]. Direct multiplication gives z^T M z=s and ||z||^2=1+||A^(-T)B^T v||^2>=1. The Rayleigh principle yields lambda_min(M)<=s/||z||^2<=s. Rotation preserves eigenvalues, so lambda_min(W)<=lambda_min(S) in every case. The PSD condition is inherent in the residual Gram construction, not an added assumption. No comparison for arbitrary indefinite residuals is asserted.

Threshold probabilities. Put eps=1/(4d^2), t=1/(2d^2), q=P(lambda_min(S)<=eps), and r=P(lambda_min(W)>=3eps). Since S=(m/d)U and Z_m=m^2 lambda_min(U), q=P(Z_m<=m/(4d))>=P(Z_m<=beta/4)>=p0 sqrt(beta)/2. The residual conditional probability given H is the same q. Also r=P(Z_d>=3/4)>=P(Z_d>=1)>=p0. Both bounds apply because m,d>=N(a). These formulas retain positive dimension m=d-T and the scaling m/d.

Error bound. Let p=P(|L-lambda_min(W)|>=eps), jointly over W,R, and b=P(L>=t). On {L>=t,lambda_min(S)<=eps}, the PSD comparison gives lambda_min(W)<=eps=t-eps, so the error is at least eps. Conditioning on H gives p>=q b. On {L<t,lambda_min(W)>=t+eps}, the error exceeds eps, so p>=r-b. Consequently b>=r-p, p>=q(r-p), and p>=qr/(1+q)>=qr/2>=p0^2 sqrt(beta)/4=c sqrt(beta). The dimension threshold is uniform over algorithms. This establishes the original existential positive-constant Theorem 10(a) scope, accuracy, and algorithm coverage. The local witness c is not a verification of the printed formula c_wish=p0^2/(2 sqrt(2)); the unspecified universal constant in the original claim may be chosen as c. A NEW independent Reviewer must check this complete local bridge.

assumptions: Exact full-vector responses for one sampled W.
Algorithm randomness is independent of W; queries may be adaptive and randomized.
The algorithm uses at most T queries, where T is a nonnegative integer with T<=floor((1-beta)d).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Sample X in R^{d by d} with independent N(0,1/d) entries and set W=XX^T. The algorithm accesses this fixed W through v in R^d mapped to Wv and returns a real scalar L estimating lambda_min(W).
statement.parameter_domains: beta in (0,1); integer d>=d_star(beta); integer 0<=T<=floor((1-beta)d). With a=sqrt(beta)/2 and N(a) defined in the local proof, d_star(beta)=ceil(N(a)/beta) suffices.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist a universal c_wish>0 and d_star:(0,1)->N such that for every beta in (0,1), every integer d>=d_star(beta), and every algorithm satisfying the query budget, the conclusion holds jointly over W and algorithm randomness. The local repair supplies p0=exp(-3/2)/2 and c_wish=p0^2/4, witnessing the original existential constant rather than the printed proof's particular constant formula.
